From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: VPC pricing ask + committed capacity discount question

Tom — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. High level responses below; I attached a pricing worksheet and a SOW draft for procurement to review.

Quick answers up front:
1) Blended examples: We show three paths in the spreadsheet — Pilot (3 months, limited nodes + 50% platform fee credit), 12-month commit (annual prepay) and 36-month anchor (deeper platform-fee amortization + volume rebates). Each tab contains token/GPU-hour math and per-token estimates.

2) Scale discounts: Two levers we commonly use: a) committed GPU-hour prepay (tiered % discount off metered rate), and b) platform fee amortization — we can reduce platform fee by up to 40% with a 36-month committed program and minimum on-call retainer. For 12-month prepay we typically offer 15-25% discount depending on volume.

3) Support tiers:
- Standard: SLA windows (4h P1, business-hours oncall), recommended for dev/test pilots.
- Business+: 24/7 P1 response + 4h remediation target, includes quarterly runbooks.
- SRE Retainer: Dedicated SRE hours per month, guaranteed response + on-site/remote runbooks for cutover.

Procurement friction notes: we often see questions on data residency clauses, termination for convenience fees, and IP/escrow language for on-prem installers. I've highlighted recommended soft language in the SOW.

Next step: if HelioCare can share an expected monthly GPU-hour run rate band (low/likely/high) and preferred billing cadence (monthly vs annual prepay), I can run a clean commercial with three numbered options and a suggested contractual playbook.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_vpc_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_draft_HELIO_4387.docx (SOW draft)

Looping in procurement/CS to align on middle ground. Tom — a couple of practical guardrails from our side:

- For any prepay discount, we need a minimum committed node baseline to size capacity; discounts scale at 10% bands (thresholds at 1k, 3k, 6k GPU-hrs).
- Platform fee amortization is only viable if the contract includes a 12-month minimum and an SRE retainer (so we can justify the reduced shared-cost).
- For CAPEX buyers we can provide an invoice schedule that maps to milestone-based recognition (helps finance teams).

If HelioCare is open to a pilot then a 3-month paid pilot (reduced platform fee, limited GPUs) + a defined roll-to-commit clause tends to speed procurement. I can propose the numeric discount table once we get the usage bands Naomi requested.

-Rishi
VP, Enterprise Sales
